name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ENVIRONMENTALISSUES_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Chronological order of environmental conservation events and laws

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following environmental conservation events, acts, and treaties in the correct chronological order (from earliest to most recent):

(I) Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act came into force in India
(II) Montreal Protocol was signed at Montreal (Canada)
(III) Amrita Devi Bishnoi sacrificed her life protecting trees near Jodhpur
(IV) Environment (Protection) Act was passed by the Government of India
(V) Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was passed by the Government of India

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Environmental conservation in India and globally progressed from early community-led sacrifices to formal national pollution-control legislation and international treaties.

Step 2: Assigning Years to Each Event
1. Amrita Devi Bishnoi's sacrifice protecting trees near Jodhpur, Rajasthan occurred in \(1731\) (III).
2. The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was passed in \(1974\) (V).
3. The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act came into force in \(1981\) (I).
4. The Environment (Protection) Act was passed in \(1986\) (IV).
5. The Montreal Protocol was signed in \(1987\) (II).

Step 3: Ordering Chronologically
Arranging from the earliest year to the latest year gives: \(1731 \rightarrow 1974 \rightarrow 1981 \rightarrow 1986 \rightarrow 1987\).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological sequence is (III) \(\rightarrow\) (V) \(\rightarrow\) (I) \(\rightarrow\) (IV) \(\rightarrow\) (II).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ENVIRONMENTALISSUES_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Sequential stages of natural eutrophication of a lake

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following stages of natural eutrophication (aging of a lake) in the correct sequential order:

(I) Silt and organic debris pile up, making the lake shallower and warmer, and warm-water organisms supplant cold-water organisms.
(II) A young lake has cold and clear water supporting little life.
(III) Large masses of floating plants (bog) dominate, and the lake finally converts into land.
(IV) Streams draining into the lake introduce nitrogen and phosphorus, encouraging aquatic life and deposition of organic remains on the bottom.
(V) Marsh plants take root in the shallows and begin to fill in the original lake basin.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Natural eutrophication is the gradual aging of a lake over thousands of years through progressive nutrient enrichment, sediment accumulation, and ecological succession.

Step 2: Ordering the Stages
1. Initially, a young lake is cold and clear and supports very little life (II).
2. Over time, streams introduce nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, increasing fertility, encouraging plant and animal growth, and depositing organic remains on the lake bottom (IV).
3. Over centuries, silt and organic debris accumulate, making the lake shallower and warmer so that warm-water organisms replace cold-water species (I).
4. Next, marsh plants take root in the shallow margins and begin filling in the lake basin (V).
5. Eventually, the lake gives way to large masses of floating plants (bog) and finally converts completely into land (III).

Step 3: Verification of Progression
The sequence follows the physical transition from deep, cold, oligotrophic water to shallow, warm, nutrient-rich water, followed by marshland, bog, and terrestrial land.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct sequential order is (II) \(\rightarrow\) (IV) \(\rightarrow\) (I) \(\rightarrow\) (V) \(\rightarrow\) (III).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ENVIRONMENTALISSUES_SEQUENCING_Q03 - Stepwise energy flow in the natural greenhouse effect

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following events in the correct logical sequence to explain the fate of sunlight energy and the heating of Earth by the natural greenhouse effect:

(I) Earth's surface re-emits heat in the form of infrared radiation.
(II) Clouds and atmospheric gases reflect about one-fourth of the incoming solar radiation and absorb some of it.
(III) Molecules of greenhouse gases radiate heat energy, a major part of which returns to Earth's surface, heating it up again.
(IV) Almost half of the incoming solar radiation falls on Earth's surface, heating it, while a small proportion is reflected back.
(V) Atmospheric greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane absorb a major fraction of the outgoing infrared radiation.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The greenhouse effect is a radiative heat-trapping cycle in which incoming short-wave solar radiation warms Earth's surface, and outgoing long-wave infrared radiation is absorbed and re-radiated by atmospheric greenhouse gases.

Step 2: Ordering the Events
1. As sunlight reaches the outermost atmosphere, clouds and gases reflect about one-fourth of the incoming solar radiation and absorb some of it (II).
2. Almost half of the incoming solar radiation reaches and falls on Earth's surface, heating it, while a small proportion is reflected back (IV).
3. The warmed Earth's surface then re-emits heat in the form of infrared radiation (I).
4. A major fraction of this infrared radiation does not escape into space because atmospheric greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane absorb it (V).
5. The molecules of these gases radiate heat energy, a major part of which comes back to Earth's surface, heating it up once again in a repeating cycle (III).

Step 3: Verification of Cause and Effect
Incoming solar interaction in the upper atmosphere precedes surface heating, which precedes infrared emission, gas absorption, and downward re-radiation.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence is (II) \(\rightarrow\) (IV) \(\rightarrow\) (I) \(\rightarrow\) (V) \(\rightarrow\) (III).
